source_title: The Lord of the Rings Film Trilogy
continuity_scope: Peter Jackson/New Line film continuity, restricted to The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001) theatrical feature and its opening through the four Hobbits' departure from the Shire. The witness includes the prologue and early Shire/Isengard intercut only; it excludes extended-edition-only material, later films, Tolkien's books as independent evidence, games, and The Rings of Power.

work_or_witnesses.work: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
The Lord of the Rings, The Fellowship of the Ring: Screenplay

coverage_rule: Include all named individual dramatic agents directly identified in AFI's film-specific prologue/Shire-departure synopsis and needed to represent a distinct early-witness role: Galadriel, Sauron, Isildur, Elrond, Gollum, Bilbo Baggins, Frodo Baggins, Gandalf, Samwise Gamgee, Meriadoc Brandybuck, Peregrin Took, and Saruman. Peoples/species, offices, orders, the Ring, places, languages, magic, cosmology, and unnamed groups remain terms rather than nodes.
omissions: All characters first materially introduced after the Shire-departure threshold, including Aragorn/Strider, Arwen, Boromir, Legolas, Gimli, and later Fellowship members.
Elendil, who is named only as Isildur's killed father in the bounded prologue account and has no separate early-witness comparison record.
Unnamed Elves, Men, Orcs, Ringwraiths, Hobbits, Wizards, and all other collective categories.
The One Ring, fellowships/orders, species/peoples, magic, locations, languages, titles, and cosmological concepts as character nodes.
Tolkien's books, extended-edition additions, The Two Towers, The Return of the King, games, The Rings of Power, and all non-Jackson continuities.
content_cautions: AFI uses source-summary descriptions such as Hobbit, Elf, Orc, Mortal Men, disfigured, and corrupted. This pass preserves only necessary film terminology and does not translate it into real race, ethnicity, nationality, disability, body, medical, or moral-essentialist categories.

The selected witness includes combat, killing, imprisonment, threats, and source language about corruption. Records avoid detailed violence, death recap, disability/mental-health diagnosis, or a conclusion that any fictional people are inherently good or evil.
Gendered titles such as lord, king, wizard, and queen are source-native fictional titles only. They are not claims about real social gender, authority, or identity.
Adaptation differences are recorded as scope boundaries rather than corrected against the books or other screen continuities.
uncertainties: AFI's public synopsis is a detailed official-reference account, not an authorized scene transcript; character claims are limited to direct synopsis wording and exact film-witness segment labels.

The exact practical Shire-departure boundary is the early four-Hobbit journey after Gandalf's instructions. No material after that early departure is imported merely because AFI's whole-film synopsis continues.
Performer and voice credits corroborate roles only; all character ontology and narrative claims are grounded in the film synopsis, not inferred from casting.
evidence_basis: AFI identifies the 2001, 178-minute New Line Cinema feature and provides film-specific prologue/Shire plot and role evidence. Google Books bibliographically identifies the contemporaneous New Line Cinema screenplay publication. No fan wiki or Wikipedia was used.
